facts.text: Yellowknife Bay was deployed at Gale Crater during Curiosity (MSL) in 2013.

Yellowknife Bay was the first major science target. Curiosity found mudstone containing clay minerals, sulphate minerals, and the chemical elements needed for life: carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulphur. This discovery fulfilled the mission's primary goal: confirming that Mars once had environments habitable for microbes.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Contained mudstone with all six elements essential for life (C, H, N, O, P, S) plus clay minerals — fulfilling the mission's goal of confirming ancient habitability.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Gale Crater.
Yellowknife Bay is where the habitability question was answered; Curiosity's drill holes there are among the most scientifically important marks on Mars.
